1: QUALIFICATION OF CANDIDATES Every candidate for municipal office who files a notice of candidacy as set forth herein shall meet the constitutional and statutory qualifications for holding the office being sought, including, without limitation, those stated in the Georgia Election Code, O.C.G.A.
3: QUALIFICATION FEE: Not later than February 1 of any year in which a general primary, nonpartisan election, or general election is to be held or, in the case of any special election held pursuant to this Ordinance, at least thirty-five days prior to such special primary or election, the governing authority shall fix and publish a qualification fee. Such fee shall be 3 percent of the annual salary of each office or such other fee as may be set forth in O.C.G.A. § 21-2-131, as may be amended from time to time.
4: TERMS OF OFFICE: All municipal officers elected in the biennial elections shall serve a term of four years. Said term shall commence on January 1 following the year of the election.
7: VACANCY: In the event that the office of mayor or of councilor shall become vacant for any cause whatsoever, the mayor and council, or those remaining, shall notify the public of the vacancy by advertising said vacancy in the legal organ for Harris County, Georgia and said vacancy in office shall be filled by the remaining members of the council until the next regularly held election. Such election and qualifications of candidates therefor shall be held in accordance with the procedure established by this Ordinance and applicable state law for regular elections.
8:
EFFECTIVE DATE: This Ordinance shall take effect from and after the date of its passage and ratification by the Mayor and Town Council of the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia.

ATTEST: This is the true Ordinance passed by the Council of the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia on the 12" day of April, 2021.
